author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list shows the first page for a page number below 1
summary: Opening the owner list with a page number below 1 (for example /owners?page=0) currently renders the error page. The owner list must treat any page below 1 as the first page and respond with the normal listing.
acceptance_criteria: given a request for the owner list with page 0, when it is opened, then the response is HTTP 200 and shows the normal owner listing for the first page
given a request for the owner list with a negative page, when it is opened, then the response is HTTP 200 and shows the normal owner listing for the first page
given a page below 1, when the listing renders, then it shows the same owners and the same current-page indication as a request for page 1
non_goals: page values that are not numbers
page numbers beyond the last page
the veterinarian directory's paging, which the request does not name
notes: PRD updated: REQ-OWN-005 added under Owner records (narrative sentence, anchor, one Done-when bullet); no Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Observed cause: the owner search handler converts the requested page to a zero-based index as page - 1 with no lower bound, so page 0 or below becomes a negative page request that fails and reaches the error page. The single test name is one data-driven test covering page 0 and a negative page. The veterinarian directory probably has the same fault but was not named by the owner; left open for a separate intake.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by the OwnerController Contracts row (system-design.md § Contracts; REQ-OWN-005 now joins it) and architecture-principles.md § DDD building blocks, Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the clamp belongs in the owner search handler. Cause verified by reading OwnerController.processFindForm (grep, weaker basis than the IDE oracle): the page parameter reaches findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, which builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize) with no lower bound; a negative index throws IllegalArgumentException and reaches the error page. Normalize once at the top of the handler (page below 1 becomes 1) so the same normalized value feeds both the repository page request and the currentPage model attribute, satisfying the 'same current-page indication' criterion. No new type, constant, or module.
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc via the existing @WebMvcTest(OwnerController.class) slice in OwnerControllerTests (the sanctioned transport double, CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): reuse the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository in OwnerControllerTests. It is a framework stub because the @WebMvcTest slice loads no JPA context and the test class already establishes this double; adding a real repository would change the test's layer. No new stub type is introduced. Stub findByLastNameStartingWith to return a multi-owner page so the list view renders rather than the single-owner redirect.

Entry point binding: no new entry point; GET /owners keeps binding page as a request-scoped int and Owner as the existing search-form object. Non-numeric page values stay out of scope (prd-entry non_goals).

patterns.description: processFindForm already normalizes its other request input (lastName null to empty, strip) at the top of the handler; the page clamp sits alongside it
existing MockMvc list-page test shape to mirror in the data-driven theOwnerListShouldShowTheFirstPageForAPageBelowOne (page 0 and a negative page)

risks.risk: Clamping only the repository call leaves currentPage rendering 0 or a negative number, breaking the third acceptance criterion
risks.mitigation: Reassign the normalized page before both uses; assert model attribute currentPage equals 1 and verify the repository received page index 0 (architecture-principles.md § Web controller: normalization is binding at the request)

risks.risk: Scope creep into VetController, whose paging helper has the same shape
risks.mitigation: Out of scope per prd-entry non_goals; leave VetController untouched

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. The only design-doc write is REQ-OWN-005 added to the OwnerController Contracts row in docs/system-design.md. No Known Defects row is added because the defect is fixed in this slice. The VetController paging helper has the same unguarded page - 1; product-requirements-expert has already flagged it for a separate intake.

findings.description: New helper aPageOfSeveralOwners() (added by this slice) constructs the second owner with a raw `new Owner()` call instead of a named factory. testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction requires new/modified tests to wrap production construction behind a factory from the start ("A slice adding a test writes it behind one from the start"); the flagged construction is confirmed at conventions-map's reported line 104 (`return new PageImpl<>(List.of(george(), new Owner()));`).
findings.fix: Add a small anonymous-owner factory (e.g. `anOwner()`) that returns a uniquely-identified, irrelevant Owner, and use it in place of `new Owner()` in aPageOfSeveralOwners().

findings.description: verify(this.owners).findByLastNameStartingWith(anyString(), argThat(pageable -> pageable.getPageNumber() == FIRST_PAGE_INDEX)) restates an outcome the behavioral assertions already cover. In OwnerController.processFindForm (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerController.java:99-123) the same `currentPage` local both feeds the repository's PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) and the model's `currentPage` attribute, so a missing clamp would make PageRequest.of receive a negative index and throw before the handler returns -- the earlier `.andExpect(status().isOk())` and `.andExpect(model().attribute("currentPage", FIRST_PAGE))` assertions already fail in that case. The verify() call asserts an internal interaction (mocking policy: interactions are asserted only where the interaction itself is the contract) without adding coverage no state assertion already gives.
findings.fix: Drop the verify(...) call; the status() and model().attribute("currentPage", ...) assertions already prove the repository was queried against the clamped page.

approved_aspects: Test placement is correct: REQ-OWN-005's clamp is a request-normalization rule inside processFindForm, which system-design.md:95 assigns to OwnerController, and testing-principles.md's pyramid section states normalization the design assigns to the web controller is tested at the web level -- the new test correctly stays a MockMvc-based web-layer test rather than being extracted for a unit test.
Naming follows the BDD school (testing-principles.md § Test Naming): theOwnerListShouldShowTheFirstPageForAPageBelowOne states the outcome, not the handler method name.
@ParameterizedTest with @ValueSource(ints = {PAGE_ZERO, NEGATIVE_PAGE}) avoids a copy-paste pair of tests for the two below-first-page inputs.

Three-tier data naming is followed: PAGE_ZERO, NEGATIVE_PAGE, FIRST_PAGE, FIRST_PAGE_INDEX are role-named constants with no bare literals in the new test's assertions (verified via conventions-map, which flagged only named-constant-bearing lines).

coverage-map --feature REQ-OWN-005 shows the slice's one Done-when bullet has its declared test present (theOwnerListShouldShowTheFirstPageForAPageBelowOne), and ./gradlew test passes with the new test green.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner list page below 1 to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production method in OwnerController (a constant plus a Math.max clamp feeding two existing call sites), one test file, and two mechanical doc edits adding the REQ-OWN-005 anchor, bullet, and contracts-row id; nothing sensitive or security-surface.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the hunk: Math.max(page, 1) points the right way, and the clamped value feeds both PageRequest.of(page - 1) and the currentPage model attribute, so page 0 or negative no longer reaches PageRequest.of with a negative index (previously an IllegalArgumentException). Pages at 1 or above, the empty-result and single-owner redirect branches, and lastName normalization all behave as before.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized MockMvc test drives page 0 and -1 through real dispatch and asserts 200, the list view, currentPage 1, and the listing. Without the clamp, PageRequest.of(-1) throws before the handler returns, so the test would fail against a broken implementation. The empty-result and redirect branches with a low page are untested, but the one clamp line sits in front of all of them.

reviewer_hedging.note: Code-quality approved cleanly with cited file:line aspects. Test-reviewer's two autofix findings (a raw new Owner() and a redundant verify under tested-as-spec) were fixed and re-approved with citations and no recommendations. I checked that dropping the verify loses no coverage, because status().isOk() already fails when the clamp is missing. The null security and doc reviewers match the low-risk focused plan.

scope_deviation.note: The change touches only the /owners list handler named by the requirement. Zero build retries, consultations, and design revisions. The fix delta changed only test construction and assertions, with no behavior change on other routes.

rationale: A small, correctly directed clamp in one handler, with a web-level test that would fail without it and clean re-approval after test-only fixes. Glance at OwnerController.processFindForm to confirm the Math.max line, then merge.
